message.content: Trade impacted the pharaoh's powers in ways that I can explain. You can see how it strengthened his authority, because it brought him rare goods, allies, and prestige. We should remember that the people honored him, yet they relied on the wealth he brought home. His officials organized the caravans, and their loyalty made the state stronger. If trade failed, however, his power shrank, since it cut off his access to materials. The pharaoh used trade to reward vassals, to punish rivals, and to project his image abroad. It was not only commerce; it was power. They understood that the pharaoh's reach extended beyond the Nile. His enemies noticed the weapons and luxury items which came by trade. His priests celebrated the returns, and his army benefited from better equipment. You should remember that the pharaoh's power depended on what his traders could bring back. In the end, their cargo determined the kingdom's fate.
